Ostris AI Toolkit diffusion-model training server — the GUI on port 8675 plus the CLI trainer
(`ai-toolkit-train <config.yml>`). Clones ai-toolkit at a PINNED COMMIT (upstream publishes no
tags at all, so a commit is the only pinnable ref), resolves its dependency set with pixi
(torch cu130 + the git-pinned diffusers revision that carries Z-Image), builds the
Next.js UI, and supervises the UI server and its job worker as two services. The mutable state —
configs, datasets, output — lives in the `ai-toolkit` volume; the application stays in the image
at /opt/ai-toolkit. Ships a Z-Image LoRA example config that trains on ostris/Z-Image-De-Turbo
and infers on Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo. Each piece is verifiable: the cloned tree at the pinned
commit, a torch that reports a CUDA device, a diffusers whose ZImagePipeline exists, the
built UI entrypoints, the example config, and the live UI on port 8675.

## Services

- `ai-toolkit-ui`
- `ai-toolkit-worker`

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | clone ai-toolkit at the pinned COMMIT into the image-owned app directory |
| `run` | build the Next.js UI so the supervised launch is immediate |
| `run` | hand the app tree to the image user so the UI can write its own runtime state |
| `run` | keep the upstream example configs aside — the live config dir becomes a volume symlink |
| `run` | install the shipped Z-Image LoRA example config |
| `run` | write the CLI trainer wrapper so a job never depends on which python is first on PATH |
| `run` | write the ONE state-splice + schema helper both services source |
| `run` | write the UI start script |
| `run` | write the start script for the job worker |
| `check` | the source tree is the PINNED commit, not whatever the default branch was that day |
| `check` | the image interpreter imports torch and the build-time CUDA stack |
| `check` | the pinned diffusers actually carries ZImagePipeline — the whole Z-Image path depends on it |
| `check` | the Z-Image model handler ai-toolkit will use for arch=zimage is importable |
| `check` | the UI was built, so the supervised launch does not build anything at start |
| `check` | the Prisma client was GENERATED — it is a build artifact, not an npm dependency |
| `check` | the shipped Z-Image LoRA example config is present in the image |
| `check` | the CLI trainer wrapper execs the image interpreter |
| `check` | the live UI answers on the toolkit port |
| `check` | the state tree is SPLICED into the volume, not left in the image |
